searchText: If anyone was curious, here's what disk usage by client pair looks like on Ropsten right now. ``` 159G ropsten-nimbus-besu 159G ropsten-teku-besu 160G ropsten-lodestar-besu 160G ropsten-prysm-besu 161G ropsten-lighthouse-besu 161G ropsten-teku-nethermind 162G ropsten-lodestar-nethermind 162G ropsten-nimbus-nethermind 163G ropsten-prysm-nethermind 164G ropsten-lighthouse-nethermind 229G ropsten-teku-geth 230G ropsten-nimbus-geth 230G ropsten-prysm-geth 231G ropsten-lodestar-geth 232G ropsten-lighthouse-geth 263G ropsten-lighthouse-erigon 263G ropsten-lodestar-erigon 266G ropsten-prysm-erigon 266G ropsten-teku-erigon 272G ropsten-nimbus-erigon ``` interesting thanks, is that besu with bonsai tries? and do you have any data on bandwidth usage? Yes, that's with bonsai. Total bandwidth usage when all clients are fully synced is ~10MB/s with some peaks ~20MB/s. That's actually taken from total traffic on my WAN interface, but the bulk of that is client testing. Restarted the Geth instance on the database shown from yesterday, still no CL, and it now seems to have imported some blocks and reports > Local chain is post-merge, waiting for beacon client sync switch-over... Yet > > [eth.getBlockByNumber(12350689).hash, eth.getBlockByNumber(12350689).totalDifficulty] > ["0xfbebe3ed657b0da33faa04f9800d873975decaeadd7fcc106f1c93f8293b6918", "0xb191d3a6f11962"] // https://ropsten.etherscan.io/block/12350689 [this block] and https://ropsten.etherscan.io/block/12350690 both pre-TTD > > eth.getBlockByNumber(12350689 + 1) > null Presumably this is intentional, but it seems odd. There's a ~25 block gap between that and TTD as accessible by `getBlockByHash` and `getBlockByNumber`, and yet it seems to know, well, a correct block to stop at anyway: > INFO [06-20|18:41:05.853] Legacy sync reached merge threshold number=12,350,713 hash=4e8451..5809f6 td=50,001,647,293,494,169 ttd=50,000,000,000,000,000
